related_questions.question: What is the 3:5-10 rule for ETF?
related_questions.snippet: The 3-5-10 rule (also known as the 3-5-10 limits) is a regulatory guideline for ETFs and other investment funds that restricts the amount they can own in another fund's voting shares. The breakdown is: 3% limit: A fund can't acquire more than 3% of the outstanding voting shares of another registered investment company.

related_questions.question: What ETF tracks the Dow Jones Industrial Average?

text_blocks.snippet: The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) is the primary ETF that tracks the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA). DIA aims to replicate the performance of the 30 blue-chip stocks included in the DJIA. It provides investors with a convenient way to gain exposure to the entire Dow Jones Index as a single security.
Here's why DIA is the go-to ETF for tracking the Dow:

list.title: Direct Replication:
list.snippet: DIA's structure is designed to closely mirror the DJIA's performance, making it a reliable choice for tracking the index.

list.title: Liquidity and Accessibility:
list.snippet: As a well-established ETF, DIA is widely traded and easily accessible to investors.

list.title: Cost-Effective:
list.snippet: It offers a cost-efficient way to invest in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

list.title: Single Security Investment:
list.snippet: DIA allows investors to invest in all 30 DJIA stocks through a single purchase.

list.title: Historical Performance:
list.snippet: DIA has a long track record of tracking the DJIA accurately.

text_blocks.snippet: While other ETFs may offer exposure to a broader range of US stocks, DIA remains the top choice for investors specifically seeking to track the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
